title: The Anatomy of Autosave
summary: This reel explains that autosave is a complex system rather than a simple status label. It details the technical and design patterns required to maintain data integrity and user trust, including debouncing, state machines, and conflict resolution.

transcript.text: "Saved." It wasn't. Your Wi-Fi died mid-word.
Nothing saves on every keystroke. A timer starts when you pause, resets when you type.
Silence for 800 milliseconds, then one clean write.
That pill is a state machine. Typing, saving, saved, offline, error.
Users trust the pill more than the feature. Never let it lie.
Offline, every edit joins a local queue. A badge counts what's waiting.
Reconnect and the queue drains in order, oldest first.
Two tabs, one document. Last write wins means someone's hour disappears.
Merge the changes or warn. Never overwrite in silence.
Closing with work unsaved, the browser blocks the tab and asks.
One ugly dialog beats an afternoon retyped.
Autosave is a system. Follow for more UX engineering. Now save this one manually.
